_purpose: Sponsorship and TV/broadcast deals are the business-management layer of the sim, separate from match results. Teams choose which sponsorship tier to pursue; the league office (instructor) allocates TV revenue by a fixed formula. Money flows into each team's budget and can be spent on trades/free agents, but never raises the salary cap itself.
sponsorship_system: draft-and-negotiate, mandatory -- see engine/negotiation.py. Sponsors are organized into sponsorship_categories (Kit/Apparel, Beverage, Financial Services, Airline, Automotive, Technology), mirroring how a real club has exactly one jersey sponsor, one kit manufacturer, one official airline, etc. EVERY team must sign exactly one brand per category by the end of the Sponsorship Draft (sponsorship_categories_required in league_config.json) -- this is not optional. Multiple teams may hold the same brand (Nike sponsors many real clubs at once; qty is a league-wide cap on how many teams total, not an exclusivity lock). SPONSORS PAY TEAMS: there is no cost to sign -- season_revenue flows into the team, full stop, matching how real sponsorship deals work. In turn order (same shape as the player draft, cycling through all 6 categories), a team targets an available brand in whichever category they're filling and makes ONE ask (base / more_revenue / looser_clause, at Modest/Bold/Very Bold intensity), resolved instantly against the team's Negotiating Leverage. An unsuccessful bold ask means the sponsor walks -- the team simply tries a different brand in that same category, or accepts base terms elsewhere; a category can never go unfilled.

clause_enforcement.description: The performance clause is not flavor text -- it is a real revenue-at-risk condition, checked ONCE at the end of the season (the final round). Each clause level sets its OWN rank threshold the team must hit to keep the money -- a strict clause demands a genuinely strict standard (top 5), a loose clause only asks for an easy one (top 15). Miss your specific deal's threshold and that deal claws back a flat 20% of its revenue, regardless of which clause it was -- the clause you negotiated determines how HARD the bar is to clear, not how much you lose if you miss it. This is evaluated PER DEAL -- each sponsor AND a team's Local TV Deal alike, same table, same mechanic: a team holding a strict-clause sponsor, a loose-clause sponsor, and a standard-clause Local TV deal could clear two of those three bars while missing the third, and only lose money on the one it missed.
clause_enforcement.notes: Thresholds (top 5 / top 9 / top 14) are set for the current 18-team league -- roughly top 25% / 50% / 75% of the table -- rescale proportionally if team count changes. 'None' has no threshold and is never penalized, full stop. The penalty is a ONE-TIME 20% deduction from that specific sponsor's already-booked revenue, applied once at season end -- never applied twice to the same deal, and never applied at all to a deal that clears its threshold.

tv_deal_formula.description: League-wide broadcast revenue pool, split at midseason (after the round-robin's halfway point) and again at season end. Modeled loosely on real sports-league media-rights revenue sharing: a shared base payment plus a performance/market-size multiplier -- the same tension between competitive-balance goals and star-driven ratings that real leagues negotiate.
tv_deal_formula.standings_bonus: Top team at split time: +1,000,000. 2nd: +600,000. 3rd: +300,000. Bottom 3 teams: +0 (no penalty beyond missing the bonus).
tv_deal_formula.star_power_bonus: If a team's average starting-XI Star Power ranks in the league's top 3 at split time, add +500,000 (broadcasters pay for star wattage independent of the standings) -- this can stack with the standings bonus.
tv_deal_formula.midseason_split_timing: After round 3 of the 17-round regular season (18 teams, round-robin) -- adjust proportionally if team count changes.

local_tv_deal_formula.description: A per-team regional broadcast contract, separate from and additional to the league-wide national TV deal above -- modeled on how real clubs also carry an individual local/regional media deal that varies hugely by market size, on top of a shared national split. Assigned once, right after Draft Day (engine/generate_local_tv_deals.py -> data/local_tv_deals.json), and fixed for the whole season like a real regional broadcast contract -- not renegotiated mid-season.
local_tv_deal_formula.market_tiers: Every team is randomly assigned exactly one of five market tiers, split as evenly as possible across the league and drawn reproducibly from season_seed: Major Market (strict clause), Large Market (strict clause), Mid Market (standard clause), Small Market (standard clause), Micro Market (loose clause) -- higher-value markets carry a stricter clause, the same pattern Sponsorship's brand table uses. Your market tier's actual base rate is not publicly posted -- your network rep tells you the number face to face when you sit down to negotiate, the same convention Sponsorship uses for its own brand base revenue.
local_tv_deal_formula.star_power_modifier: If a team's average starting-XI Star Power ranks in the league's top 3 at split time, its Local TV Deal pays +15% that round -- same top-3 threshold as the national deal's star bonus, scaled off the team's own base (proportional) rather than a flat dollar add, since a Major Market base and a Micro Market base already differ so much in size.
local_tv_deal_formula.payout_timing: Paid out at the same midseason split point as the national TV deal (after Round 3 of the 17-round regular season) -- one TV Revenue Day covers both national and local money at once.
local_tv_deal_formula.salary_cap_note: Local TV revenue flows into the team's budget like any other revenue; it never raises the salary cap itself.
local_tv_deal_formula.negotiation: Right after Draft Day, every team negotiates its Local TV Deal live, in class, against a rotating peer playing the network rep (engine/generate_tv_negotiation_rotation.py pairs everyone once, no repeat partners; an odd team count leaves one bye, filled by the instructor). Exactly like Sponsorship, TWO separate things are on the table -- same mechanic, same functions in engine/negotiation.py. Revenue: take the market-tier Base rate exactly (guaranteed, zero risk), or Negotiate to land anywhere from -10% to +10% of it, set by your Negotiating Leverage (built from your roster average Star Power, plus a standings bonus once the season starts). Your market tier's exact base rate is not publicly posted anywhere -- your network rep tells you the number face to face at the start of the negotiation, the same convention Sponsorship uses for its own brand base revenue. Clause: a separate ask -- push for a looser clause than your market tier's base clause, at Modest/Bold/Very Bold intensity, gated by the same leverage number against a required threshold; an unsuccessful ask can walk away (clause stays at base, no revenue impact). The commission: whenever a negotiated rate lands away from base -- in EITHER direction -- that gap is ALSO credited immediately (not at the Round 3 split) as bonus revenue to whichever team played the network rep. Above base rewards the negotiating team's win; below base (a good deal for the network) rewards the rep instead, same size commission, mirrored direction -- same either-direction logic as a sponsorship commission. Landing exactly at base earns nobody a commission. This negotiation sets the RATE and the CLAUSE only; the money itself is still paid at the Round 3 split above, with the Star Power modifier still applied on top then, and the clause is checked once at season end exactly like a sponsorship clause (see clause_enforcement above -- the same rank thresholds apply to Local TV deals). The League-Wide (National) TV Deal is not part of this exercise -- it is a shared, formula-only split with no natural second party to negotiate against.

playoffs.format: No bracket games are played. The top finishers in the final regular-season standings (see the qualification line marked on the dashboard, and the bonus table below) are recognized as Playoff Qualifiers -- a season-ending designation, not a separate elimination tournament.
playoffs.bonus_notes: Paid once, at season's end, to every team that finishes inside the qualification line -- not stacked or tiered by seed. 1st place and 6th place both earn this bonus equally; regular-season standings already reward finishing 1st over 6th through the Ranking component of the Season Scorecard.

trade_rules.deadline: Trades may be proposed through Round 6 of the 17-round regular season. No trades are permitted in Rounds 7-17 or at any point after -- this prevents last-minute roster stacking right before the playoff-qualification picture is set, the same reason real leagues carry a trade deadline.
trade_rules.salary_cap: A trade is only valid if BOTH teams remain at or under salary_cap (see league_config.json) after the trade completes.
trade_rules.cash_considerations: Teams may include cash (from their budget, not a salary-cap item) as part of a trade package.
trade_rules.approval: All trades are submitted via the Trade Proposal form and require instructor (league office) approval before taking effect -- this is the checkpoint for grading trade rationale and for vetoing collusive or lopsided trades.
trade_rules.mid_season_trade_day: One mandatory in-class Trade Day, held mid-season (right after the Round 3 TV-revenue split, well ahead of the Round 6 deadline). Every team is paired with exactly one partner from a published rotation (engine/generate_trade_day_rotation.py, same no-repeat pairing method as the Sponsorship Negotiation rotation) and must negotiate and submit ONE completed Trade Proposal by end of class -- real assets, or a good-faith minor swap if the two sides can't agree on more, since grading is on the negotiation and rationale, not on landing a 'good' trade. An odd team count leaves one team unpaired; the instructor fills in as that team's trade partner, the same convention already used for the Sponsorship Negotiation rotation's bye. This is a floor, not a cap: the ordinary voluntary trade window stays open before and after Trade Day, through Round 6.
